title: Foundations of GenIR
extended_summary:
This chapter presents a conceptual overview of modern generative AI as it relates to information access systems. Rather than reporting an empirical study, it explains how large language models and other generative models change the design space for information retrieval and information synthesis. The paper frames two major paradigms: information generation, where models create tailored outputs directly from user prompts, and information synthesis, where models combine retrieved external information to produce grounded responses.

The chapter first reviews foundational technical components of generative AI, including transformer architectures, scaling laws, training stages such as pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from human feedback, as well as prompt optimization. It then discusses multimodal understanding and generation, including how language models support image and video tasks.

A substantial portion of the chapter focuses on retrieval-augmented generation and related information synthesis methods, such as naive and modular RAG, optimization of retrieval and generation, retrieval planning for composite information needs, generative retrieval, and domain-specific modeling. The discussion is broad and theoretical, aimed at explaining opportunities, tradeoffs, and open problems rather than evaluating a specific intervention with a learner population. The main conclusion is that generative AI can improve information access both by directly generating content and by synthesizing external knowledge, but many challenges remain around hallucination, controllability, retrieval integration, and domain adaptation.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI / large language model systems that create text, images, or other outputs from prompts, and can also synthesize external information via retrieval-augmented methods.
identified_tools.use_case: The chapter discusses generative AI at a foundational level, focusing on information generation and information synthesis in information access systems, including ChatGPT, Bing with RAG, Midjourney, and related LLM-based methods.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical chapter about generative AI foundations and information access, not an empirical study of a K-12 educational tool or intervention. No research design, sample, or outcome data are reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The chapter has broad conceptual relevance to generative AI systems, but it reports no measured educational outcomes, so there is no direct evidence of impact in K-12 literacy or related settings.
